content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Status: missing** — no insurance clause exists anywhere in the Agreement.

**What I found:**
- A full-text search for "insurance" returned zero hits, and the section outline has no insurance heading.
- The miscellaneous provisions run continuously from § 13 (Term) through § 30 (Force Majeure) and then straight into the signature block, confirming the gap is a genuine omission rather than a clause filed under an unexpected heading.

**Why this is material and not a minor sub-element:**
TrueLink is squarely the kind of vendor the rule targets. It hosts the Web Site, receives and uploads **Client Content** (§ 1.b), and transmits and archives **Credit Data** — raw borrower and loan-applicant creditworthiness data from TransUnion, Equifax and Experian (§ 1.d). That is personal financial data, so zero insurance falls into the rule's walk-away territory, missing both the preferred package and the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).

I also checked whether the gap was cured indirectly, and it is not — if anything the surrounding bargain makes it worse. TrueLink's indemnity in § 12.b has no coverage requirement behind it, and § 12 caps its liability for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 at just 12 months of hosting and support fees. So in a data incident we would have neither a meaningful contractual cap nor an insurer to look to.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** New § 31 inserted after § 30, before the signature block, at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request, held through the term plus one year. I drafted it using the Agreement's own defined terms (Client Content, Credit Data) so the cyber coverage ties explicitly to what TrueLink actually processes. The comment offers the fallback limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) as a landing zone if TrueLink resists the amounts.
